message.datacircuit.port_cleared: Data links removed at this port.
message.datacircuit.selection_cancelled_: Data wire selection cancelled because a block was broken.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.hold_shift: Hold Shift for DataCircuit helper text
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.title: DataCircuit Analysis
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.create_read: Create-ready: keeps circuit port and gate rules explicit.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.generic: A DataCircuit device that works in an explicit data-link network.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.data_wire_n: Wall, floor, or ceiling data port. Right-click two ports to create a direct wire link.
Example: right-click node A, then node B, to link only those two ports.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.data_signal: Basic sender that only emits 0/1 bit data.
Example: each right-click sends 0 or 1 along the wire.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.data_lamp: Output device. Stays lit while at least one connected input remains ON.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.data_lamp.e: Example: BIT 1 turns it on, BIT 0 turns it off. Number/text/RGB do not directly light it.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.number_inpu: Right-click to enter a number and send it through the wire.
Example: sending 42 transmits NUMBER 42 to wires and Create display devices.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.text_input: Right-click to enter text and send it through the wire.
Example: sending HELLO transmits TEXT HELLO for text arithmetic.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.rgb_selecto: Right-click to choose an RGB color or enter a HEX value and send it through the wire.
Example: sending #33AAFF shows RGB color data on the wire.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.add_block: Adds numbers, joins text with a space, and mixes RGB colors.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.subtract_bl: Subtracts numbers, removes the first matching text segment, and subtracts RGB channels.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.multiply_bl: Multiplies numbers. Text times a number repeats the text; text times text outputs a red ! error.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.divide_bloc: Divides numbers. Text division removes every matching text segment. Division by zero outputs 0.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.power_block: Raises numbers to a power. Text and RGB output a red ! error.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.conversion_: Number conversion: BIT=0/1, NUMBER=its value, HEX=base 16, RGB=24-bit integer. TEXT falls back to parsed number or 0 only for non-text operations.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.and_gate: Logic gate: both side inputs must be ON for the front output to turn ON.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.and_gate.ex: Example: 1 AND 1 = 1; either side at 0 outputs 0.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.or_gate: Logic gate: either side input can turn the front output ON.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.xor_gate: Logic gate: front output turns ON only when the two side inputs differ.
tooltip.datacircuit.analysis.not_gate: Logic gate: inverts the back input and sends the result through the front output.
datacircuit.ponder.tag.data_circuits.des: Explicit data wires, Boolean logic, and data circuit devices for Create-style automation.
datacircuit.ponder.data_wire_node.title: Explicit Data Wire Nodes
datacircuit.ponder.data_wire_node.text_1: Data Wire Nodes are mounted ports, not redstone dust.
datacircuit.ponder.data_wire_node.text_2: DataCircuit wires are explicit links. Nearby blocks do not receive data unless a wire node is actually connected.
datacircuit.ponder.shared.datacircuit_li: DataCircuit wires are explicit links. Nearby blocks do not receive data unless a wire node is actually connected.
datacircuit.ponder.shared.datacircuit_cr: Create: DataCircuit is ready for Create packs. Wire links are world-position based, so moving contraptions will need dedicated integration next.
datacircuit.ponder.data_signal_source.te: Right-click a Data Signal Source to toggle a 0/1 signal.
datacircuit.ponder.data_lamp.title: Reading Data Outputs
datacircuit.ponder.data_lamp.text_1: Data Lamps react only to their connected data network.
datacircuit.ponder.data_lamp.text_2: If multiple inputs feed one output, the lamp stays on while any input remains on.
datacircuit.ponder.number_input.title: Number Input
datacircuit.ponder.number_input.text_1: Right-click to enter a number, then send it as NUMBER data.
datacircuit.ponder.number_input.text_2: Example: 42 travels through the connected wire.
datacircuit.ponder.text_input.title: Text Input
datacircuit.ponder.text_input.text_1: Right-click to enter text, then send it as TEXT data.
datacircuit.ponder.text_input.text_2: Example: HELLO can be shown on Create displays or used by text arithmetic.
datacircuit.ponder.rgb_selector.title: RGB Selector
datacircuit.ponder.rgb_selector.text_1: Right-click to choose or type a HEX color.
datacircuit.ponder.rgb_selector.text_2: Example: #33AAFF travels as RGB data and is drawn in that color.
datacircuit.ponder.add_block.title: Add Block
datacircuit.ponder.add_block.text_1: Left and right wire nodes are inputs; the front node is the result output.
datacircuit.ponder.add_block.text_2: Adds numbers, joins text with a space, and mixes RGB colors.
datacircuit.ponder.subtract_block.title: Subtract Block
datacircuit.ponder.subtract_block.text_1: Left and right wire nodes are inputs; the front node is the result output.
datacircuit.ponder.subtract_block.text_2: Subtracts numbers and removes the first matching text segment.
datacircuit.ponder.multiply_block.title: Multiply Block
datacircuit.ponder.multiply_block.text_1: Left and right wire nodes are inputs; the front node is the result output.
datacircuit.ponder.multiply_block.text_2: Multiplies numbers. Text times a number repeats the text.
datacircuit.ponder.divide_block.title: Divide Block
datacircuit.ponder.divide_block.text_1: Left and right wire nodes are inputs; the front node is the result output.
datacircuit.ponder.divide_block.text_2: Divides numbers and removes every matching text segment.
datacircuit.ponder.power_block.title: Power Block
datacircuit.ponder.power_block.text_1: Left and right wire nodes are inputs; the front node is the result output.
datacircuit.ponder.power_block.text_2: Raises numbers to a power. Text and RGB output an error.
datacircuit.ponder.and_gate.title: AND Gate
datacircuit.ponder.and_gate.text_1: Attach wire nodes to the left and right sides for inputs.
datacircuit.ponder.and_gate.text_2: Both side inputs must be on before the front output turns on.
datacircuit.ponder.and_gate.text_3: One input is on, but AND still keeps the output off.
datacircuit.ponder.and_gate.text_4: With both inputs on, the output finally turns on.
datacircuit.ponder.or_gate.title: OR Gate
datacircuit.ponder.or_gate.text_1: Attach wire nodes to the left and right sides for inputs.
datacircuit.ponder.or_gate.text_2: Either side input can turn the front output on.
datacircuit.ponder.or_gate.text_3: OR turns on as soon as either input becomes 1.
datacircuit.ponder.or_gate.text_4: The second input can also be on; the output stays on.
datacircuit.ponder.xor_gate.title: XOR Gate
datacircuit.ponder.xor_gate.text_1: Attach wire nodes to the left and right sides for inputs.
datacircuit.ponder.xor_gate.text_2: The front output turns on only when the two side inputs differ.
datacircuit.ponder.xor_gate.text_3: XOR turns on when exactly one input is 1.
datacircuit.ponder.xor_gate.text_4: When both inputs match, XOR turns the output back off.
datacircuit.ponder.not_gate.title: NOT Gate
datacircuit.ponder.not_gate.text_1: NOT uses the back as input and the front as inverted output.
datacircuit.ponder.not_gate.text_2: With no input, NOT starts on. A true input turns its output off.
datacircuit.ponder.not_gate.text_3: When the back input becomes 1, the inverted front output becomes 0.
